messages:
ops_incident_bot: PAGER — Severity P1: detected sudden tail latency spike in us-west-2 ingress -> routing layer. p95 jumped to ~450ms, p99 to ~2.1s. Several streaming requests stalled. Auto-pager sent to #incidents and @oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: thanks for the page. I'm grabbing it. quick TL;DR: router LB is skewing to a small set of shards, causing hot partitions and queuing. markers: sustained CPU on those backends + queue growth on router-proxy.

marie.ryan: I'm on infra. seeing multiple LB weight updates in the last minute from the routing-policy service. examples in logs: 
```
INFO router.policy: applied weights {shard-101:0.88, shard-42:0.92, shard-7:0.02} by controller=policy/v2026-03-14
```
Those weight sums shouldn't be >1 after normalization — looks like a math bug.

ahmed.khan: confirmed. p95/p99 graphs: 
- baseline p95 ~80ms, p99 ~280ms
- spike window 20:02-20:12 UTC: p95 ~450ms, p99 ~2.1s
streaming stalls: token gaps observed where connection remains open but no tokens returned for 3-6s.

tess.li: customer reports coming in. customer_ops: which tenants are impacted?

customer_ops: so far we have three customers reporting increased latency and partial streaming stalls: acme-pay, fincore, edulog. severity P1 from their side because real-time UI is affected. We put fincore on an incident bridge.

jules: summary of quick mitigations I want to try: 1) rollback the routing-policy to v2026-03-13-stable 2) enable eager_fallback threshold temporarily 3) drain/backoff the hot shards 4) create alert on weight-normalization anomaly. any objections?

marie.ryan: +1 to rollback first — that should stop new skewed updates from landing. I'll run a rollback command now.

marie.ryan: running:
```
# rollback routing policy to last-known-good
policyctl apply --policy ingress-routing --from stable --to v2026-03-13-stable --force
```

router-bot: Applying policy rollback: ingress-routing -> v2026-03-13-stable. Rolling update started (3 zones). Progress: 0/12 -> 4/12 -> 9/12 -> 12/12

oncall-sre: while rollback rolls, enabling eager_fallback for model groups heavily affected (text-gen streaming). This reduces chances of long tail by falling back to smaller quantized model quickly.

tess.li: I've updated the policy flag: 
```
curl -X POST https://config.local/flags/eager_fallback -d '{"region":"us-west-2","enabled":true,"ttl":600}'
```

ahmed.khan: after rollback and eager_fallback we see immediate improvement in routing distribution; p95 trending down to ~120ms, p99 to ~340ms in the last 60s. streaming stalls reduced but a few connections still showing gaps.

jules: good. we should still mitigate hot shards at the LB layer. marie, can you weight-shift shard-42 and shard-101 down and ramp up more nodes for that shard group?

marie.ryan: doing a controlled weight adjust to flatten distribution. command: 
```
routectl adjust-weights --shard shard-42,shard-101 --set 0.15 --region us-west-2 --dry-run=false
```

router-bot: weight adjustments accepted. New weights applied. Rebalancer scheduling 6 additional endpoint attachments to reduce queuing.

oncall-sre: monitoring traces — queue latency on the router proxies is dropping. hook into trace span #trace-7f9b for streaming stalls; the root cause span shows the routing decision waited on lock for 800-1200ms when weights were skewed.

customer_ops: acme-pay confirms improvement from their side. fincore still seeing occasional token gaps on long-lived streams (~5% of requests). They requested we keep them updated.

ahmed.khan: we should capture the exact policy diff that caused the explosion. initial investigation: rounding bug in normalization function in routing-policy service (floating point cumulative >1). Patch ready: 
```
- total = sum(weights)
- normalized = [w/total for w in weights]
+ total = max(sum(weights), 1e-6)
+ normalized = [w/total for w in weights]
```
This prevents division by tiny numbers / accidental amplification.

jules: nice. plan of record: 1) rollback (done) 2) weight flatten + rebalancer (done) 3) enable eager_fallback (done) 4) hot-shard drain until capacity stabilizes 5) ship the normalization patch to routing-policy + unit tests 6) add alerts for weight-sum deviation > 0.05 from 1.0 7) postmortem and customer comms.

tess.li: I'll draft customer comms for acme-pay/fincore/edulog. Include root cause overview and mitigation steps we took + ETA for a permanent fix.

marie.ryan: hot-shard drain is in progress: draining 2 nodes currently, expected finish 20:42 UTC. Rebalancer is attaching capacity.

oncall-sre: handover note: I'm going to hand off the incident bridge to jules at 20:49 UTC — jules will own the active mitigation and patch rollout. I'll remain available for escalation.

jules: taking over 20:49 UTC. current status: p95 ~95-130ms, p99 ~300-360ms (stable but above baseline). streaming stalls reduced to ~1% of long-lived streams. continuing: coordinate patch rollout (canary in staging -> us-west-2 canary -> full), add monitoring, schedule postmortem.

router-bot: patch job queued: routing-policy v2026-03-14-fixnorm -> will deploy to staging canary in 10m.

customer_ops: fincore asked for an SLA credit evaluation; capture exact windows: impact start 20:02 UTC, mitigation effective ~20:12 UTC, residual degradation until 20:30 UTC.

jules: noted. action items logged on the bridge:
- marie: follow up on weight normalization PR + tests (owner)
- ahmed: add alert rule for weight-sum deviation (owner)
- tess: customer comms + credits draft (owner)
- jules: coordinate canary + postmortem (owner)

marie.ryan: quick follow-up: we found two policy controller instances with stale config caches that applied outdated normalization logic during a short window when a controller leader election happened. We'll harden leader election path and add a config reload sanity check.

oncall-sre: thanks team. jules will run the postmortem template and we will schedule a follow-up ops review tomorrow. closing the immediate page — we'll keep the thread updated with the patch rollout and any customer escalations.

customer_ops: acme-pay and edulog both acknowledged the improvement and will watch for regression. fincore will remain on hold until we confirm the patch.

ops_incident_bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity downgraded to P2 (residual impact). Patch queued for rollout.

jules: ending bridge for now at 20:55 UTC. keeping this thread live for updates. thanks everyone.
